name: Provider and asset routing
observations: OpenMontage is AGPL-3.0; LICENSE identifies GNU Affero General Public License version 3 at lines 1-2 and the preamble describes copyleft terms at lines 10-18.

Provider discovery is registry-driven: ToolRegistry.discover walks the tools package and registers modules (tools/tool_registry.py:118-139); provider and capability catalogs group discovered tools (tools/tool_registry.py:153-159, 212-230). The user-facing provider menu excludes selector aggregators and reports runtime, dependencies, status, provider matrices, source menus, and operation status (tools/tool_registry.py:249-314).

BaseTool distinguishes local, local-GPU, API, and hybrid runtimes (tools/base_tool.py:86-93), and standardizes ToolResult fields including success, data, artifacts, cost, duration, model, seed, and from_cache (tools/base_tool.py:132-145). Dependency checks use command, environment-variable, and Python-module declarations (tools/base_tool.py:488-510).

ImageSelector and VideoSelector auto-discover concrete providers by capability rather than hard-coding a provider list (tools/graphics/image_selector.py:1-5, 216-230; tools/video/video_selector.py:1-5, 300-309). Both expose provider-neutral inputs and rank mode; successful results include selected tool/provider, selection reason, provider score, tool skills/context, and alternatives (tools/graphics/image_selector.py:255-278, 358-373; tools/video/video_selector.py:368-438).

Routing supports exact tool, hosting-provider, model/model-id/model-name, operation, and custom-workflow constraints through filter_explicit_route (tools/provider_routing.py:6-54). Video routing additionally filters operation readiness, supports allowed providers, and honors preferred providers only within a configurable score gap; selection is keyed by tool name so distinct tools sharing a provider remain reachable (tools/video/video_selector.py:440-523, 569-631).

VideoSelector prevents an image-only fallback for image-to-video and reference-to-video operations, while allowing image fallback for text-to-video; this is explicitly tested (tools/video/video_selector.py:320-334; tests/tools/test_video_selector_routing.py:235-256). Local reference images are uploaded only when the selected provider schema requires image_url; an Ark route preserves the local path and does not use the FAL uploader (tools/video/video_selector.py:403-420; tests/tools/test_video_selector_routing.py:289-323).

Stock providers use a common StockSource protocol with stable name, availability check, search, and download methods. Candidate records normalize source, source ID, landing URL, download URL, media kind, dimensions, duration, creator, license, tags, thumbnail, and extra metadata; clip IDs are source plus source ID (tools/video/stock_sources/base.py:1-35, 43-80, 102-141). Adapters are intentionally dumb: API-shape/licensing/download normalization is separated from corpus indexing, retrieval, ranking, deduplication, and acceptance judgment (tools/video/stock_sources/base.py:12-21).

CorpusBuilder skips unavailable sources when no source list is pinned, but explicitly fails rather than silently substituting when requested sources are unavailable (tools/video/corpus_builder.py:260-299). Stock transport errors are intended to propagate from adapters and be handled per-source; tests document known adapter exceptions as remaining defects (tools/video/stock_sources/base.py:121-126; tests/tools/test_stock_source_adapters.py:80-115, 195-220).

The asset manifest schema requires version 1.0 and per-asset id, type, path, source_tool, and scene_id; optional provenance includes provider, license, original_url, model, prompt, seed, cost, resolution, duration, subtype, and generation summary (schemas/artifacts/asset_manifest.schema.json:1-36). The schema rejects additional per-asset and top-level properties (schemas/artifacts/asset_manifest.schema.json:55-61).

Pipeline manifests declaratively bind stages to artifacts, preferred/fallback/required/optional tools, review focus, success criteria, human approval, and permitted extensions (schemas/pipelines/pipeline_manifest.schema.json:76-151, 183-195). The loader resolves a named YAML file, validates it against the JSON schema, lists definitions, computes required tools, and enforces extension permissions (lib/pipeline_loader.py:49-70, 152-162, 197-228).

Representative manifests require asset stages to produce asset_manifest and validate file existence. Animation explicitly requires selector tools rather than direct provider calls and requires skills-read metadata; cinematic requires real video for motion-required beats and separates source selects from generated support assets (pipeline_defs/animation.yaml:169-221; pipeline_defs/cinematic.yaml:161-207). Documentary montage routes through direct_clip_search/corpus_builder/clip_search and requires one unique picked clip per slot plus provider/original_url/license provenance (pipeline_defs/documentary-montage.yaml:86-117).

OpenMontage has a literal resolveAsset helper only in the Remotion composer, not in provider routing: it resolves absolute URLs unchanged, otherwise prefixes a relative asset path with the configured public base URL (remotion-composer/src/lib/resolveAsset.ts:1-20). Components use it at render time for scene media, audio, and overlays (remotion-composer/src/CinematicRenderer.tsx:78, 248, 432; remotion-composer/src/Explainer.tsx:398-534, 886-892).

The content-addressed asset cache is opt-in via OPENMONTAGE_ASSET_CACHE, defaults to ~/.openmontage/asset_cache, uses an atomic JSONL manifest, file locking, immutable copies, and LRU eviction (lib/asset_cache.py:23-59, 93-130, 194-218, 231-317). BaseTool cache admission excludes stochastic tools, requires output_path, and only caches deterministic or seed-pinned single-artifact calls; cache hits restore structured metadata and repoint local output references (tools/base_tool.py:291-310, 313-340, 343-403).

MPS currently implements one local deterministic cinematic renderer, one optional caller-supplied hosted renderer hook, and an SVG scene-card fallback; the order and explicit fallback semantics are in scripts/hybrid_video.py:1-12, 216-244. Its production manifest records only local-cinematic, hosted-provider, and static-svg-fallback decisions (scripts/production_manifest.py:19-79).

MPS MPVE persists storyboard/job/render metadata, deduplicates canonical requests, and reports provider, artifact, duration, aspect ratio, audio, fallback assets, errors, and quality gates (scripts/mpve_engine.py:131-177, 180-228; scripts/hybrid_video.py:35-56, 247-250). MPS documentation states the hosted hook is not a configured provider and that narration/TTS/captions remain host/provider extensions (docs/mpve-report.md:60-67).

MPS tests verify local-first ordering, no hosted call when local succeeds, provider manifest serialization, and genuine MP4 properties, but do not test asset manifest resolution or a multi-provider selector (tests/test_hybrid_video.py:29-64; tests/test_production_manifest.py:21-35).
inferences: OpenMontage treats provider routing as a capability-level orchestration problem: selectors normalize a shared contract, filter unsupported routes, score candidates, and delegate to a concrete tool; provider-specific API shape remains behind each tool.

The stable boundary for clean-room integration is not a copied provider implementation but the observable contracts: capability/provider/runtime metadata, explicit route constraints, normalized ToolResult, auditable selection metadata, asset-manifest provenance, and explicit fallback reporting.

OpenMontage separates source acquisition from asset acceptance: stock adapters normalize candidates and provenance, while corpus/retrieval/agent stages decide what to keep. This reduces provider coupling but means a clean-room MPVE must define its own acceptance and provenance policy rather than assume a source adapter ranks quality.
The asset manifest is the durable join between generation/source tools and composition. resolveAsset is a render-time path-to-URL adapter, not a provider resolver and not a license/provenance system.

OpenMontage's cache design implies that provider identity, tool version, model, declared idempotency inputs, determinism, and single-artifact output are necessary to safely avoid repeat paid calls; stochastic cloud video should not be silently cached merely because a seed field exists.

Pipeline manifests are governance as much as configuration: motion promises, source-vs-generated distinctions, human approvals, skill-read requirements, and no-silent-fallback rules are expected to constrain routing decisions.

MPS is intentionally a narrow local-first vertical slice, not an OpenMontage-equivalent provider layer: it has no concrete external provider adapters, no capability selector, no stock-source abstraction, no asset-manifest schema, and no render-time URL resolver.
unknowns: No literal resolveAsset symbol exists in provider or asset-routing modules; the only implementation is the Remotion helper. Its full runtime base URL configuration and deployment behavior were not inferred beyond the helper source and call sites.

The audit does not establish whether every OpenMontage provider tool consistently validates remote URLs, licenses, MIME types, dimensions, or downloaded bytes; those guarantees vary by adapter and were not exhaustively sampled.

The selector score weights and runtime availability can change with environment configuration and tool metadata; static source inspection does not establish the selected provider for every possible machine state.

Known stock adapters archive_org, wikimedia, and pond5_pd are marked as expected failures for transport-error propagation, so the documented ideal boundary is not uniformly implemented (tests/tools/test_stock_source_adapters.py:108-115).

MPS's optional hosted_renderer callable has no concrete adapter contract for authentication, upload, polling, retries, remote task IDs, URLs, licensing, or provenance (scripts/hybrid_video.py:216-240; docs/mpve-report.md:65-67).
MPS job JSON is persisted but the in-memory job index is not reconstructed after restart, and no remote object storage or retention policy exists (docs/mpve-report.md:60-67).
The current MPS working tree has pre-existing modifications in README.md and scripts/logic_engine.py; this audit did not alter them and they are outside the subsystem scope.
contracts: A concrete provider must expose stable tool identity, capability, provider, runtime, dependency/status, input schema, output/artifact behavior, cost/runtime estimates, and fallback/skill metadata through BaseTool and registry discovery (tools/base_tool.py:409-465, 478-526; tools/tool_registry.py:118-159).

Selectors must accept provider-neutral requests, constrain candidates by explicit preferred tool/host/model/operation when requested, and fail clearly when no compatible provider remains (tools/provider_routing.py:6-54; tools/graphics/image_selector.py:255-278; tools/video/video_selector.py:368-394).

Successful selection must preserve selected tool/provider, reason/score, alternatives, and relevant tool context in the result; direct provider-specific fields may be stripped rather than silently passed to incompatible tools (tools/graphics/image_selector.py:306-373; tools/video/video_selector.py:421-438).

Motion-required operations must not degrade to an image-only fallback; any degraded fallback for non-motion text-to-video must be explicit in result metadata (tools/video/video_selector.py:320-334, 436-438; tests/tools/test_video_selector_routing.py:235-256).

Every materialized asset must have a stable ID, type, local path, source tool, scene ID, and where applicable provider/license/original URL/model/prompt/seed/cost metadata; composition should consume the manifest rather than provider internals (schemas/artifacts/asset_manifest.schema.json:7-36).

Pinned unavailable stock sources must cause a structured failure rather than silent substitution; unpinned source selection may use currently available sources (tools/video/corpus_builder.py:260-299; tests/tools/test_documentary_governance.py:72-107).

A source adapter's empty result means a genuine no-match response, while transport errors should remain distinguishable and propagate to the per-source orchestrator (tools/video/stock_sources/base.py:121-126; tests/tools/test_stock_source_adapters.py:195-220).

A cache may bypass a provider only when opt-in, reproducibility/determinism, idempotency fields, output path, and single-artifact conditions are satisfied; cache hits must report cached status and preserve structured output metadata (tools/base_tool.py:291-310, 313-403).

Pipeline policy must preserve declared motion promises, provenance, review gates, and human approvals; a missing runtime or provider must be a surfaced blocker, not a silent engine/provider swap (pipeline_defs/cinematic.yaml:198-207; pipeline_defs/documentary-montage.yaml:164-177; tests/tools/test_documentary_governance.py:142-188).

For MPS, MPVE must receive structured context only after MPS decides a video intervention is appropriate, and it must return control for written teaching/mastery; MPVE must not invent triggers or declare mastery (docs/mpve-integration.md:5-8, 38-42; skills/mpve/SKILL.md:8-18, 30-40).
mps_gaps: MPS has no capability-level image/video/provider selector, no registry discovery, and no explicit host/model/operation filtering; its provider choice is a fixed local-first chain with an opaque caller-supplied hosted callback (scripts/hybrid_video.py:216-240; scripts/production_manifest.py:51-79).

MPS has no asset_manifest schema or per-asset provider/license/original_url/source_tool/scene_id contract. Its fallback_assets list is only a list of generated paths and does not provide durable source provenance (scripts/hybrid_video.py:35-56,241-250; scripts/mpve_engine.py:214-225).

MPS has no resolveAsset-equivalent for composition-time local/remote media URL normalization; the local renderer draws from storyboard data and the hosted hook receives a storyboard plus output path only (scripts/hybrid_video.py:183-210,216-240).

MPS has no stock-source protocol, corpus builder, candidate normalization, pinned-source failure semantics, or provenance-preserving real-footage route; current MPVE output is generated local visuals or static SVG fallback (scripts/hybrid_video.py:106-180,241-244; docs/mpve-report.md:64-67).

MPS provider metadata lacks OpenMontage-style runtime/dependency/status, operation readiness, cost/runtime estimates, model catalogs, alternatives, and selection rationale. The production manifest records provider order and selected boolean but not candidate scores or normalized route inputs (scripts/production_manifest.py:19-79).

MPS has no opt-in content-addressed cache keyed by tool/version/idempotency fields and determinism. MPVE deduplicates canonical requests at the job level only; it does not prevent repeated paid asset/provider calls behind a hosted adapter (scripts/mpve_engine.py:139-160; lib/asset_cache.py:1-18 as comparison).

MPS fallback semantics are explicit at the render result level, but there is no operation-aware guarantee equivalent to OpenMontage's motion-required no-still-substitution rule; this should be added if hosted or stock routes are introduced.

MPS does not reconstruct the in-memory job index across restarts and has no durable external task resume, authenticated storage, or remote artifact URL contract, limiting production use of external providers (docs/mpve-report.md:60-67).
clean_room_recommendations: Define a small independently written MPVE provider interface with capability, provider, runtime, availability, supported operations, model/host identity, cost/runtime estimates, and structured execute results; keep all vendor SDK/API code behind adapters and do not import OpenMontage modules or source text.

Add an operation-aware selector only if MPS needs more than its current local/hosted/fallback chain. Require explicit route inputs for preferred provider, host, model, and operation; return selected adapter, alternatives, rationale, and normalized request metadata.

Introduce an MPS-owned asset manifest with stable asset IDs, scene IDs, local artifact paths, source adapter, provider/model, license, original URL, prompt/seed, cost, and media dimensions/duration. Validate it before composition and reject missing files or missing provenance for sourced media.

Implement an MPS-owned resolveAsset-style path adapter at the composition boundary that handles local paths and approved remote URLs without conflating URL resolution with provider selection, downloading, licensing, or trust decisions.

If real footage is added, use a source protocol with normalized candidates and provenance, distinguish empty search results from transport failures, and reject unavailable explicitly pinned sources rather than silently substituting another source.

Preserve motion promises: a motion-required request must not be downgraded to still cards or images without an explicit failure/degraded result and caller-visible explanation. Keep static SVG as a clearly typed fallback artifact, never as an MP4 claim.

Add opt-in, content-addressed caching only for reproducible single-artifact routes, including adapter/version/model/operation/input identity and seed where applicable; never cache stochastic hosted video solely because an API exposes a seed.

Extend the production manifest with actual candidate decisions, selected route, route constraints, fallback transitions, provenance, cache status, remote task IDs, and artifact URLs/paths; retain MPS's existing explicit audio and fallback flags.

Add contract tests for no hosted call after local success, explicit provider failure, operation-aware fallback exclusion, pinned-source failure, asset-manifest validation, local/remote asset resolution, provider metadata preservation, cache hit/miss behavior, and restart-safe external task polling.

Keep the current MPS pedagogical boundary: MPS remains responsible for intervention triggers, learner context, follow-up teaching, and mastery; MPVE remains a media capability and must not independently trigger or grade learning.
